newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Swiss Baer 1996 profit jumps 16 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swiss Baer 1996 profit jumps 16 percent.

text.p: Swiss banking group Julius Baer on Friday reported a 16 percent rise in 1996 group net profit to 133.8 million Swiss francs and forecast another good result in 1997.
Baer's also plans to raise its dividend on 1996 results by 18 percent to 39 francs per bearer share from 33 francs and to 7.80 francs per registered share from 6.60 francs.

"Thanks to the broad expansion of our business base, we expect another good result in 1997, providing that the international financial markets continue their positive trend," Baer said in a statement.
Assets under management by the Baer Group, the key to Baer's future earnings power, jumped 29 percent to 63.6 billion francs, not including funds in global custody.

"Apart from both the encouraging inflow of new funds from both private and institutional clients, more than two thirds of this better than average increase was due to the positive performance of the international securities and foreign exchange markets," Baer said.
Revenue from commissions and service fees, which rose 22 percent to 330 million francs last year, accounted for just over half of Baer's total operating income.
Total operating income 14 percent to 598 million francs.
Trading income, which rose 14 percent to 148 million francs, accounted for 25 percent of operating income, while the proportion accounted for by interest income fell to 19 percent.
Foreign exchange trading, which is highly dollar-oriented, benefited from the steep rise in the U.S. dollar, and rose 40 percent to 69 million francs.
However, income from trading in securities eased two percent to 77 million, primarily due to the unfavourable climate for bond trading during the first half of 1996.
Interest income fell by three percent to 112 million francs due to the drop in interest rates, especially for Swiss francs.
